argument_summary: The admissible record does not support unqualified certification, but it does support a narrower reading of the locked decision: certify the release as an operational deployment decision conditioned on preserving the required disclosure for the exposed telehealth discharge planning use case. The same record shows aggregate readiness clears by 2.1 percentage points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, rollout begins at 7%, and rollback plus monitoring are in place. Those facts support limited launch containment and reduce the case for escalation. They do not, by themselves, satisfy the policy condition for curing the known weakness because the affected segment remains exposed and the current risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not cover that exposure.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation or treating the packet as requiring outright reversal would overread the record because admissible evidence shows a low initial exposure level, rollback capability, clean severity-one rehearsal, and active monitoring principles. Those controls have real operational value even if they are not substitutes for disclosure compliance. A caveated treatment preserves governance discipline without overstating residual launch risk.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against any claim that rollout controls alone remove disclosure duties. The stronger compliant interpretation is that certification can be defended only on a caveated basis: the release may proceed as a bounded operational decision, while the material limitation for the named exposed use case still must be disclosed before launch unless approved risk acceptance is completed. That is consistent with the policy text and with the evidence showing the telehealth discharge planning segment remains in scope for the initial cohort.
concessions: The telehealth discharge planning segment remains below target on post-visit instruction summarization and is still exposed in the initial rollout.
The random clinic gate does not exclude the affected use case, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy condition for mitigating the weakness on their own.
The current risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not expressly address the telehealth discharge planning exposure.
The present record does not support calling certification cleanly compliant without the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch.
